skill.name: quality-verify
skill.description: Verify a final deliverable against quality standards before delivery, using six review dimensions and a scored readiness rubric.
skill.summary: Final quality gate for code, documentation, and other deliverables before handoff.
skill.author: AbeJitsu

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences and an inline path reference in SKILL.md. The skill provides a quality verification rubric and does not instruct command execution, network access, secret access, or reconnaissance. No semantic security findings were found.

static_findings.snippet: - Quality is subjective - but consistency is objective (did it follow their standards?)

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 61-74 are a Markdown code fence around scoring text, not Ruby or shell execution. There is no command invocation or user-controlled input.
The flagged text is a Markdown fence and nearby process prose. The JavaScript example begins at line 90 and uses repository API calls, not command execution.
The JavaScript example calls standardsRepository.getStandards and verification helpers. It does not use child_process, shell commands, or backtick execution.
Line 101 is a closing Markdown fence. It does not execute code or instruct the assistant to run an external command.
The inline backticks mark a documentation path reference. They do not represent shell substitution, command execution, or unsafe file access.
The flagged block is a JSON output example in Markdown. It contains no shell commands, process execution, or user input interpolation.
The snippet is a Markdown fence closing a JSON example and surrounding prose. It describes quality criteria and contains no executable command path.

content.value_statement: Final checks often miss consistency, security, or completeness gaps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a scored review before delivery.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates deliverables across completeness, correctness, consistency, performance, security, and maintainability.
Applies a scoring rubric with thresholds for ready, minor fixes, and major revision.
Adapts checks to project standards through the referenced StandardsRepository pattern.
Lists specific issues with critical, major, and minor severity groupings.
Gives delivery recommendations based on the final quality score.
limitations: It depends on the model's ability to inspect the submitted deliverable.
It does not run tests or scanners by itself.
It cannot verify external facts without current sources.
It needs clear user standards for strict project-specific checks.

use_cases.title: Final Code Review
use_cases.description: Check a feature before handoff for completeness, runtime risk, security basics, and maintainability.

use_cases.title: Documentation Handoff Check
use_cases.description: Score API or product documentation for completeness, consistency, clarity, and missing examples.

use_cases.title: Release Readiness Gate
use_cases.description: Apply one rubric before delivery so reviewers see issues, severity, score, and recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Final Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-verify to review this deliverable. Score each applicable dimension and tell me whether it is ready to deliver.

prompt_templates.title: Standards-Based Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-verify with our project standards. Identify missing requirements, score each dimension, and list required fixes before delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-Artifact Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-verify on the feature and its documentation. Compare behavior, examples, edge cases, and security expectations before recommending delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Strict Release Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-verify as a release gate. Apply strict scoring, separate critical, major, and minor issues, and recommend ship or revise.

output_examples.input: Review a React dropdown component before handoff.
output_examples.output: The component is ready after minor fixes. The review notes strong completeness, a keyboard navigation gap, and one missing edge case test.

output_examples.input: Check API endpoint documentation for release.
output_examples.output: The documentation needs revision. It lacks error response examples, has inconsistent parameter names, and should be updated before delivery.

output_examples.input: Validate a generated project report before sharing it.
output_examples.output: The report is ready to share. It meets the requested structure, uses consistent formatting, and has no major accuracy issues.

best_practices: Provide the full deliverable and any project standards before running the skill.
Ask for separate evidence for each critical or major issue.
Use the score as a decision aid, not as the only review authority.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill as a replacement for automated tests.
Do not accept vague issues without specific locations or examples.
Do not force every dimension when it does not apply to the deliverable.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews a final deliverable for completeness, correctness, consistency, performance, security, and maintainability.

faq.question: Does it execute tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance unless you also ask the assistant to run tools.

faq.question: Can it review documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can score docs for completeness, correctness, consistency, clarity, and maintainability.

faq.question: How does scoring work?
faq.answer: It averages applicable dimensions, then applies deductions for critical, major, and minor issues.

faq.question: Does it need project standards?
faq.answer: Project standards improve accuracy, but it can fall back to general quality practices.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it as the last check before sharing code, docs, plans, or other deliverables.
